facts.text: I know that bacteria can be classified as viruses, pathogens, microorganisms, non-pathogens, or fomites.
I know that a microorganism that causes disease is a pathogen.
I know that Neisseria gonorrhea is normally cultured on Thayer-Martin agar.
I know that Escherichia coli normally resides in the intestinal tract.
I know that darkness does not help a microorganism grow.
I know that appropriate oxygen and/or carbon dioxide would interfere with the growth of a pathogen.
I know that a microorganism that requires oxygen to grow is an aerobe.
I know that optimum growth temperature is defined as the temperature at which a microorganism grows best.
I know that the convalescent period is when symptoms have subsided and the patient is regaining health.
I know that throat swabs are collected to diagnose Streptococcus.
I know that the source of the specimen should be indicated on a swab for C&S to assist the lab staff for billing purposes.
I know that activated charcoal in transport medium helps maintain a neutral pH by neutralizing fatty acids and absorbing toxic substances.
I know that urine for C&S can be collected using a clean catch MSU.
I know that giving instructions for a clean catch MSU includes cleansing from front to back for female patients.
I know that a cutaneous mycosis is collected by performing a skin scraping.
I know that septicemia is detected by collecting blood.
I know that blood culture collection does not require keeping the specimens at room temperature until they are incubated.
I know that a stool specimen for C&S must not be contaminated with urine, toilet water, or toilet paper.
I know that a specimen for pinworm testing is collected first thing in the morning before a bowel movement.
I know that a container required for pinworm exam is scotch tape/glass slide or a sticky paddle.
I know that cocci are round-shaped bacteria.
I know that pyogenic means producing pus.
I know that pyrogenic means producing fever.
I know that staphylococci are arranged in clusters in chains or pairs (two of the above).
I know that Staphylococcus aureus causes boils, wound infections, meningitis, abscesses, and UTI (everything except one listed option).
I know that streptococci are in chain formation.
I know that lactose fermenter bacteria are cultured on MacConkey agar.
I know that blood is the body fluid collected to detect septicemia.
I know that Streptococcus causes throat infection.
I know that Group A Streptococci cause rheumatic fever.
I know that some bacteria form a hard-protective covering resistant to heat and chemicals called a capsule.
I know that bacilli may be spore formers.
I know that blood agar media is enriched and can show hemolytic activities using 5% sheep blood.
I know that cylindrical shaped bacteria with flexibility and movement are vibrios.
I know that bacteria that resemble a comma are vibrios.
I know that blood is collected to detect Neisseria meningitides.
I know that on a microscope, the diaphragm adjusts the amount of light coming into the lens system.
I know that total magnification of oil immersion objectives and a 10X ocular is 1000X.
I know that the scanning objective allows the largest field of vision.
I know that when putting away a microscope after use, you should not unplug the microscope.
